items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: I was going to say, you couldn’t have had many friends that were boys that were your age that would like go, “So what do you think of James P. Johnson?” ... Yeah, right. Is he a pitcher for the Philadelphia Phillies?

ctx.x: Right. He was very florid and fluid and you know, romantic. And my father was — he wasn’t a musician, my mother wasn’t a musician. No one had any instruments in the house. But I got stung. And as the years went on I started reading every book I could. And one summer I’d just read Hemingway, Storm Jamesen and a number of others that had nothing to do with music. And another summer it was all the beat generation. But other summers it was just music. Just all the things I could get on jazz and pop and everything…
I was going to say, you couldn’t have had many friends that were boys that were your age that would like go, “So what do you think of James P. Johnson?” © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

Yeah, right. Is he a pitcher for the Philadelphia Phillies? I knew every baseball player so I was pretty good there, and you know, was a basketball kid. But I had this other passion. So on weekends I’d go to the Grosvener Library, the downtown library, and they would have these magazines down in the subbasement. And I would get them called up, and they’d get to know who I was so as soon as I walked in I’d go, “I want the Jazz Reviews” you know, “of all the ones I didn’t read last week.” And I’d take notes on…
